setupTask.text:
Read the repository's manifests, CI configuration, compose files, test configuration and README. Find the units whose tests run on their own (a package, a service, a crate) and describe each as a project in a review.yaml. Prove each project with try_project: it builds the project's Docker image (network allowed while installing), starts the services it lists, and runs its existing suite with no internet apart from those services. Revise until every project's suite runs, then submit the whole file with propose. propose checks that no file is owned by two projects. It runs each project changed since it was proven, so there is no need to try every project again after editing another one. Source files outside every project come back to you once, by folder: put those a project tests under its owns or uses, and arnx lists the rest under uncovered.

Found: python (pyproject.toml), $HOME

The YAML has these keys:
version: 1
services: {<name>: {image: <image>, env: {<NAME>: <value>}, ready: <command that succeeds once it accepts connections>}}
allow_env_names: [<names that look like secrets but hold throwaway values, such as a test database password>]
projects:
  <name>:                  # lowercase letters, digits and dashes
    root: <directory where the tests run, relative to the repository root; "." for the root>
    language: <python, typescript (also for JavaScript) or rust>
    runner: <pytest; vitest, jest, node or bun; nextest>
    image: <base image>
    install: [<shell commands run once while building, from root>]
    test_command: <a command that runs the runner directly, with the placeholder {targets}>
    services: [<names from services above that this project's tests need>]
    env: {<NAME>: <value>}   # the only variables tests see; services are reachable with their name as host
    owns: [<paths whose changes this project tests; default: its root, usually right>]
    uses: [<paths it depends on but does not own, such as a shared library directory>]
    notes: [<short facts a test writer needs: how to point the code at the database, what must be stubbed>]
    tests_dir: <optional: where arnx writes its tests, relative to root; arnx sets it from the runner's configuration (vitest include, jest roots and testMatch, pytest testpaths), so set it only when try_project says its folder is not picked up>
uncovered: [{path: <path pattern>, reason: <why no project tests it: no tests, scripts, unsupported language, infrastructure>}]   # source files only: leave docs, data and configuration out

Paths in owns, uses and uncovered work like .gitignore: a trailing / names a directory, a leading / anchors to the repository root, * stays in one directory and ** crosses directories.

Rules:
- Never put real secrets in env. A variable whose name contains KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD or CREDENTIAL is refused, unless its value is arnx:generated or its name is in allow_env_names (throwaway values only).
- When the tests need a secret value but no real one, write arnx:generated. arnx sets 64 hex digits (arnx:generated:base64: 32 bytes in URL-safe base64, such as a Fernet key), the same in every variable and service that uses it.
- Propose one project per unit that is tested on its own. Put shared code under uses of every project that imports it.
- Tests that fail on the current code are recorded one by one as failing today. Leave them in the suite: do not exclude tests in test_command. Fix only what the environment causes. Failures that look like the environment come back to you once; trying the project again unchanged records them with their cause.
- try_project also places a one-line test in the project's tests_dir and checks that the runner runs it. When it does not, set tests_dir to a new, empty subfolder inside a folder the configuration includes (for example __tests__/unit/arnx_generated). Never use a folder that holds the project's own tests, and do not change the project's own configuration.
- Once try_project has built a project's image, look around in it with exec (versions, files, a single test). Do not put probes in test_command: each try_project runs the whole suite.
- Do not set up tests that run in a browser (Playwright, Cypress, Storybook, vitest browser mode). arnx lists them under uncovered as browser tests.
- A web UI app (react-dom, next, vue, svelte, @angular/core, solid-js, preact, nuxt, @sveltejs/kit, astro or electron among its dependencies) gets one try at its node or jsdom unit tests. If that try fails, arnx lists it under uncovered as web UI. Do not try it again; go on with the rest.
- Stop when propose accepts the file. Then reply with a short summary of what you chose and why.
